title: Uncertainty over US tariffs keeps copper trading in a tight range
text:
Uncertainty over US tariffs keeps copper trading in a tight range
- Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.1% at $14,353 a metric ton
LONDON: Copper prices were little changed on Tuesday, trading in a tight range for a third straight session, as uncertainty over potential US import tariffs and concerns about inflation driven by higher oil prices kept risk sentiment subdued.
Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.1% at $14,353 a metric ton by 0955 GMT.
Copper, widely used in the power and construction sectors, has risen 55% since Donald Trump returned to the US presidency in January 2025, despite global demand falling 0.5% to 27 million metric tons, Panmure Liberum analyst Tom Price said in a note.
Supporting prices is a shortage of copper scrap in China, which is increasing the country’s need for refined copper through domestic inventory drawdowns, just as the US continues to import metal and build stocks ahead of potential tariffs, Goldman Sachs said.
The bank’s analysts expect copper prices to average $15,400 in 2027, up from $14,700 at the end of 2026.
The Yangshan copper premium, a key indicator of China’s demand for imported copper, climbed 0.7% to $138 a ton, its highest level in almost four years.
Meanwhile, Comex copper inventories were last at a record high of 718,199 metric tons, up from 87,241 in January 2025.
The White House has yet to decide on tariffs on refined copper, with the administration increasingly focused on affordability ahead of November’s midterm elections, Reuters reported in September, citing people familiar with the matter.
Chinese broker Everbright Futures said cautious purchasing at high prices and uncertainty over US tariffs could keep copper prices range-bound in the near term.
BHP Group and Anglo American reported declines of 19% and 5%, respectively, in quarterly copper production due to disruptions in Chile, but both companies maintained their full-year output guidance.
Among other LME metals, aluminium fell 0.8% to $2,993, zinc lost 0.7% to $3,688, lead was steady at $1,894.50, while tin gained 0.1% to $50,775 and nickel rose 0.5% to $15,600.

title: Kremlin hopes Witkoff can brief Putin soon on latest Ukrainian/European thinking on peace deal
text:
Kremlin hopes Witkoff can brief Putin soon on latest Ukrainian/European thinking on peace deal
- Putin and US envoy Witkoff are expected to meet soon to address the Ukraine peace process and other critical bilateral issues
MOSCOW: The Kremlin said on Tuesday that it hoped a meeting in Russia between President Vladimir Putin and US special envoy Steve Witkoff could be organised in the near future to discuss the Ukraine peace process and a range of “very important issues.”
Witkoff is expected to hold talks in Oslo on Tuesday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and representatives from the E4 – made up of Britain, France, Germany, and Poland. Officials from the European Union and NATO are also expected to attend.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that Witkoff could brief Putin on the position of the Ukrainians and Europeans when they met.
Putin proposes summit with Trump and Xi to discuss Ukraine deal, WSJ says
“We hope that a meeting can be arranged in the very near future, and that the American negotiators, Mr Witkoff, will be able to brief President Putin on their contacts with both the Ukrainians and the Europeans, as well as to continue the exchange of views between Washington and Moscow on a whole range of very important issues. We consider such meetings to be of great importance on every occasion; they are always timely and very substantive, and we greatly appreciate the mediation efforts of the American negotiators,” Peskov told reporters.
He did not give further details. Some US media have reported that Witkoff may meet Putin on Wednesday in St Petersburg.
A recent call between Putin and Trump produced an agreement on Russian diesel supplies, which Trump said could lower prices but which alarmed Ukraine and European allies.

title: Bavuma, Jansen lead South Africa fightback in second test
text:
Bavuma, Jansen lead South Africa fightback in second test
- South Africa staged a remarkable comeback, reaching 216/6 thanks to Bavuma and Jansen's record partnership
GQEBERHA: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma and all-rounder Marco Jansen led a record-breaking fightback to take their side to 216 runs for six wickets at lunch on the third day of the second test at St George’s Park on Tuesday.
Bavuma was 76 not out after the first session in a gritty display while big-hitting Jansen scored 72 off 71 balls in an unbeaten 106-run seventh-wicket partnership as the home side clawed their way out of a precarious position.
The partnership came off 133 balls and broke the previous South Africa record of 89 runs for the seventh wicket in a test at St George’s Park, set against England in 1896.
Bavuma to captain South Africa ODI squad against Australia
South Africa resumed on 97-5 after only 43 overs were bowled on the opening two rain-affected days with Bavuma on 41 and Wiaan Mulder on two.
Mulder was the only wicket to fall on Tuesday as he ducked into a short-pitched ball from Mitchell Starc and gloved the ball behind to slip Matt Renshaw. It was Starc’s 450th test wicket but was only given out after a review.
Australia had to do without seamer Josh Hazlewood for the first session because he did not field on Monday after falling ill and was serving penalty time before being allowed to bowl. He will be able to do so after lunch with the new ball due eight overs into the afternoon session.

title: Pakistan, Qatar agree to strengthen security cooperation
text:
Pakistan, Qatar agree to strengthen security cooperation
- Commit to work together for regional peace and stability
Pakistan and Qatar's Interior Ministers met to bolster bilateral cooperation in internal security, reaffirming their commitment to regional peace and stability and strengthening their security partnership.
- Expanding cooperation in internal security.
- Strengthening the security partnership between the two nations.
- Views on regional peace and stability.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Qatar’s Minister of Interior and Commander of the Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya), Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation in internal security.
During the meeting, the two interior ministers held detailed discussions on expanding cooperation in various internal security-related fields and agreed to further strengthen their security partnership.
The two sides also exchanged views on the prevailing regional situation and matters relating to regional peace and stability. They reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing bilateral cooperation between the interior ministries of Pakistan and Qatar.
It was decided that mutual cooperation and partnership in internal security would be further strengthened.
“Pakistan and Qatar are working together for regional peace and stability,” Mohsin Naqvi said.
The Qatari interior minister said his country attached great importance to its relations with Pakistan.

title: Where Atatürk’s legacy lives: Ankara, Baku, Nicosia
text:
For Pakistan, Turkey is one of its closest countries: an ally, a partner, a country whose history is better known here than that of many others. But even a close country may not be known in its entirety. Turkey’s secularism is neither a borrowing nor a compromise, but the principle on which Mustafa Kemal Atatürk founded the republic and which was incorporated into its constitution in 1937. For seventy years, it determined what Turkish schools, universities and the civil service looked like. For the past two decades, Turkey has been governed by a different tradition, a religious-conservative one, and beyond its borders the first tradition is not always remembered. In autumn 2026, it was brought back into focus by a dispute sparked by Azerbaijan, which approved uniform requirements for school dress in September.
The decision concerned only public schools, but it was discussed far beyond them — most loudly in Turkey, where a presidential adviser, lawmakers from the ruling party and protesters outside the Azerbaijani consulate in Istanbul called on Baku to reconsider it. For Pakistan, where the hijab is an everyday feature of school life, this reaction is understandable. But it reflects only one of the two traditions that coexist in Turkey. The other deserves no less attention.
In substance, the decision was narrower than the reaction to it might suggest. The headscarf was not included among the elements of the school uniform; the regulation concerns only public schools and only uniforms: universities, workplaces, streets and mosques remain unaffected. The same document permits national dress at school events. The country’s highest religious authority, the Caucasus Muslims Office, called the hijab an important religious obligation — and stated in the same declaration that citizens have no right to oppose decisions of the state. Azerbaijan is a secular state under its Constitution and a Muslim country in terms of its population, and these two characteristics have never been considered contradictory there.
The Turkish Republic was founded on the same principle — and although restrictions on headscarves in universities and government institutions have been lifted under the current government, the tradition on which the republic was built has not disappeared. It is represented by the Kemalist opposition, a significant part of academia, the judiciary and the military — and by a substantial part of society for whom the secular state remains part of national identity, rather than a rejection of faith.
It was from this Turkey that different assessments of Azerbaijan’s decision emerged. Theologian and columnist Cemil Kılıç urged Azerbaijan to ‘carefully preserve its secular identity’. Professor Aygün Attar, former rector of Giresun University and a member of the Security and Foreign Policy Council under the President of Turkey, suggested that Azerbaijan should not be judged ‘exclusively through the prism of Turkey’. Ömer Faruk Kocatepe, an international relations scholar and associate professor at Turkey’s National Defence University, stressed: ‘Azerbaijan is an independent state with its own history and political and social characteristics. Our brotherhood stands above current political events, disagreements and debates.’
Just how alive this tradition remains was demonstrated by Northern Cyprus, where, six months before the events in Azerbaijan, the same dispute unfolded in the opposite direction. In April 2025, the government of the Turkish Cypriot administration, which is close to Ankara, allowed female students in upper secondary school to wear headscarves in public schools. The response was the largest protests in Turkish Cypriot history: on 8 April, around thirteen thousand people marched through northern Nicosia under the slogan ‘Cyprus is secular and will remain secular’; in May, a general strike brought the north of the island to a standstill. President Erdoğan sharply condemned the protesters and promised to visit. In September, the Constitutional Court of the Turkish Cypriot administration overturned the permission following a lawsuit by the teachers’ union, on the grounds that only parliament had the authority to make such a decision. In October, Turkish Cypriots elected the leader of the secular opposition, Tufan Erhürman, as president.
In other words, Turkish Cypriots — a Turkic people, Muslims living under Turkey’s protection and with its financial support — defended secular schooling in defiance of Ankara. Six months later, Azerbaijan made the same decision and faced the same criticism from the same circles. In both cases, the dispute took place within the Turkish world itself — over what public schools should be like and who has the right to decide.
Baku’s response, delivered on 13 October by the ruling New Azerbaijan Party, addressed precisely this dispute. The party recalled that the formula ‘one nation, two states’ means one nation and two independent states, and gives neither the right to interfere in the other’s internal affairs; that Azerbaijan is a secular state under its Constitution, and that the same principle is enshrined in the Constitution of the Republic of Turkey; and that using the headscarf as an instrument of political manipulation ‘serves neither the unity of the Turkish people nor the solidarity of the Muslim world as a whole’.
The secular tradition in Turkey is neither a thing of the past nor merely an opposition position, but part of what Turkey remains: its Constitution, its universities, its military, millions of its citizens. Azerbaijan arrived at the secular state by its own path and reached the same conclusion: faith belongs to the individual, school belongs to everyone. In this sense, the autumn controversy is not a confrontation between Ankara and Baku. It continues a debate Turkey has been having with itself for a century: about the place of religion in the state, about who schools belong to, about Atatürk’s legacy. Azerbaijan’s decision merely carried that debate beyond Turkey’s borders — and Baku found both its own position and supporters among Turks themselves. For readers in Pakistan, the debate offers another perspective on the different traditions that coexist within a close partner, Turkey.
The article does not necessarily reflect the opinion of Business Recorder or its owners.
The author is journalist and analyst (Sofia, Bulgaria)

title: SECP launches Security Operations Center to strengthen cybersecurity
text:
SECP launches Security Operations Center to strengthen cybersecurity
- SOC will provide continuous monitoring of SECP’s networks, endpoints, servers and private cloud environments
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has launched its Security Operations Center (SOC) to protect critical information assets, detect cyber threats at an early stage and enable timely incident response, strengthening the regulator’s cybersecurity and operational resilience, read a statement on Tuesday.
The SOC will provide continuous monitoring of SECP’s networks, endpoints, servers and private cloud environments, read a statement.
Funded by Karandaaz Pakistan, as the implementing agency for the UK Government’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), enabled by Inara Technologies, Pakistan, and supported by REWTERZ under a Managed Security Services Provider agreement, the centre will operate in line with recognised international standards and best practices.
Chairman of the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA), Lieutenant General Muhammad Munir Afsar, inaugurated the SOC and appreciated SECP’s initiative, emphasising the importance of cybersecurity.
During a separate meeting, SECP Chairman Dr Kabir Ahmed Sidhu briefed the NADRA chairman on the commission’s IT reforms, infrastructure modernisation, and adoption of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies to improve service delivery and facilitate ease of doing business.
SECP also plans to integrate the Security Operations Centers of Capital Markets Institutions (CMIs) into a sector-wide framework for threat intelligence sharing and coordinated incident response, supporting the regulator’s envisioned role as a Sectoral Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) and Sectoral SOC.

title: HUBCO denies BYD plant delay, targets end-2026 launch: report
text:
HUBCO denies BYD plant delay, targets end-2026 launch: report
- According to the report, vehicle production will initially rely entirely on imported raw materials and components
HUBCO plans to launch its BYD vehicle assembly plant by late 2026, targeting 1,000-1,500 monthly sales. The plant will gradually localize production, introduce more models, and create jobs.
- HUBCO's BYD plant launch timeline and sales targets.
- Phased introduction of BYD models and localization goals.
- Environmental benefits and job creation from the new facility.
Hub Power Company (HUBCO) aims to bring its BYD vehicle assembly plant online by the end of 2026, targeting an initial sales run rate of 1,000 to 1,500 vehicles per month as production ramps up, management said in its annual general meeting.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL), which attended the meeting, said in its report that the company plans to introduce additional BYD models in phases.
“Management intends to introduce additional BYD models through a phased approach, targeting price segments and vehicle categories with the highest sales potential. It does not intend to launch models indiscriminately and believes competitive pricing and product quality will support market share gains,” AHL said on Tuesday.
According to the report, vehicle production will initially rely entirely on imported raw materials and components, with local content expected to increase gradually.
“The long-term objective is to localise up to 80% of the vehicle, which should improve cost competitiveness and reduce reliance on imports,” said the brokerage house
HUBCO’s management denied that the plant had been delayed and reiterated its target of bringing the facility online by the end of calendar year 2026.
It is expected to be operational “in 4-5 weeks”, Zayan Babar Khan, analyst at AHL, told Business Recorder.
The update comes as HUBCO expands its investment in the automotive sector through BYD, the Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer.
Earlier this month, Liu Xueliang, Vice President of BYD Co., Ltd., and General Manager of BYD’s Asia Pacific Auto Sales Division, in an exclusive talk to BR Research, said that the BYD manufacturing plant being established in Pakistan is “nearing its launch in the second half of 2026”.
“This is BYD’s sixth facility outside of China and has a production capacity of 25,000 units per annum, scalable to 50,000 units per annum,” said Liu, while adding that more details about the project will be shared in due course.
“This plant is expected to generate more than 1,100 jobs, advance sustainable industrialisation, and help avoid an estimated 165,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions by 2034,” he added.

title: Jesse Eisenberg, Julianne Moore bring curtain down on London Film Festival with 'The Debut'
text:
Jesse Eisenberg, Julianne Moore bring curtain down on London Film Festival with 'The Debut'
- Moore stars as Mona, a shy New Jersey housewife who is thrilled to land a role in a community theatre musical
LONDON: Actor-filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg said he wrote the lead role in his musical comedy “The Debut” with Julianne Moore in mind, praising the Oscar-winning star as “the greatest actress in the world” as the film closed the London Film Festival on Sunday.
“I just thought, this is Julianne Moore, and I will write every scene with her in mind and what she likes to do and what she’s great at,” Eisenberg, who wrote the screenplay and directed the film, told Reuters on the red carpet.
Moore stars as Mona, a shy New Jersey housewife who is thrilled to land a role in a community theatre musical.
Drawn to the experience by a longing for something missing in her life, Mona finds purpose and community through the show.
“She’s moving towards something, knowing that there’s something that she needs in her life,” Moore said. “Then that thing leads you towards yourself and towards community, which is really the most valuable thing of all.”
The film, which marks Eisenberg’s latest directing effort following his BAFTA-winning screenplay for “A Real Pain”, features seven original songs written by the filmmaker. The numbers appear in the fictional stage production “Nosy Neighbours”, a deliberately light-hearted, 1990s-inspired musical performed by a cast including “The Little Mermaid” star Halle Bailey.
Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff shot at in Mumbai, three suspects held: police
“I love songwriting, I love musical theatre music and I wrote these songs in earnest,” Eisenberg said.
Mona’s early struggles on stage test the patience of director Jerry, played by “The Holdovers” star Paul Giamatti, prompting her to adopt an increasingly committed method acting approach.
Eisenberg said Moore’s interpretation of Mona allowed him to make a “weird movie” that still felt grounded.
“She is so unusual, she’s so strange,” he said. “It allowed me to make a movie that wasn’t realistic.”
While Mona takes method acting to extremes, the “Now You See Me” star said all actors, including himself, draw on some version of the technique.
“I always wind up feeling whatever the character feels,” he said. “So if my character is miserable, I spend the shoot just miserable. But I don’t realise it’s for the character. I just think, ‘Oh God, I must be doing terribly in the movie’.”
Eisenberg, who plays a minor role in “The Debut”, said the story was inspired by his own childhood experiences in community theatre, where he discovered “a family and a home and a life” he liked.
Patrick Fabian, who plays Mona’s husband in the film, said theatre offers something increasingly rare: a chance for people to connect in person with one another.
“It brings people together, and these days, it gets them out of their screens and into the dark together to watch whatever is going on,” Fabian said. “I think that’s a real bonding thing.”
“The Debut” brought the curtain down on the 70th London Film Festival, where Ukrainian filmmaker Sergei Loznitsa’s “Imperium” won Best Film in the Official Competition.

title: UEFA demands answers from FIFA over Infantino presidency - reports
text:
UEFA demands answers from FIFA over Infantino presidency - reports
- UEFA has led calls for Infantino to resign since he proposed the now-abandoned FFE project
UEFA has formally questioned FIFA President Gianni Infantino's leadership, demanding immediate answers on projects like the FFE and the FIFA Peace Prize ahead of his re-election bid.
- UEFA's specific concerns regarding Infantino's governance.
- The controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project.
- Infantino's upcoming re-election and nomination deadline.
UEFA has sent a letter to FIFA seeking answers about Gianni Infantino’s presidency, including questions over the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project and the FIFA Peace Prize, by November 2, British media reported on Monday.
UEFA has led calls for Infantino to resign since he proposed the now-abandoned FFE project, which involved creating a company to run the commercial interests of FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, and selling a minority stake to private investors.
The 56-year-old, who is up for reelection next year, apologised to the FIFA Council last week and told attendees to submit any questions they had about his governance in writing so he could answer them at the next meeting on December 16.
However, Sky Sports and other British media reported on Monday that UEFA General Secretary Theodore Theodoridis had written to his FIFA counterpart Mattias Grafstrom seeking a swift response to 42 questions covering 12 topics.
“These questions require answers now,” Theodoridis wrote.
“They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the FIFA Council - nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them.”
Reuters has not seen a copy of the letter.
UEFA and FIFA did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.
Infantino will stand for reelection in March 2027, with a November 18 deadline looming for potential candidates to submit their nominations.

title: New Zealand plot downfall of 'incredible' India teen Sooryavanshi
text:
New Zealand plot downfall of 'incredible' India teen Sooryavanshi
- He recently won an Asian Games gold medal in Japan as India swept to the T20 cricket title in Aichi-Nagoya
New Zealand paceman Jacob Duffy expects home conditions to challenge India's 15-year-old cricket sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in the upcoming T20 series, despite his impressive power-hitting record.
- New Zealand's strategy to counter Sooryavanshi's power-hitting.
- How New Zealand's seam-friendly pitches might affect the young prodigy.
- Jacob Duffy's personal ambitions and preparations for the series.
New Zealand have done their homework on India prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and expect their home conditions will challenge the 15-year-old sensation in the Twenty20 series starting on Thursday, paceman Jacob Duffy said.
Sooryavanshi has lit up world cricket with his power-hitting, breaking a string of records in the Indian Premier League before becoming India’s youngest international in the men’s game with his debut in the T20 series in England in July.
After a slow start against England, the teenage opener became the youngest player to score a half-century in men’s international cricket when he clobbered an 18-ball fifty against Zimbabwe.
He recently won an Asian Games gold medal in Japan as India swept to the T20 cricket title in Aichi-Nagoya.
Duffy said New Zealand had been studying the left-hander in the buildup to the five-match series, which starts at Christchurch’s Hagley Oval.
“First of all, he’s an incredible talent. Obviously, he’s taken the IPL by storm and what’s amazing, he strikes it so hard but he does it so consistently,” Duffy told reporters on Tuesday.
“He’s striking at 250 (strike-rate) every game and he’s not missing out very often. So that’s incredible in itself.
“I think he played in England, so conditions will be a little bit different for him, so that’s obviously one thing for him to be challenged with.
“We’ve certainly had a good scouting session on him and got our plans as to what we want to do to him.”
India fans will be eager to see what Sooryavanshi can do in New Zealand, where the pitches tend to be seam-friendly.
Duffy said he had spoken to Hagley Oval’s head groundsman about what to expect from the wicket, hoping that it will not be a batter’s paradise like some subcontinent pitches.
“He’s from Invercargill, so he’s promised me a little bit of bounce,” said Duffy, who was born in Lumsden, a small town near the South Island city.
“As long as it’s not Hyderabad, I’m happy.”
The T20 series is the first part of India’s tour, with one-day matches and a two-test series to follow.
Otago bowler Duffy has had a big year, claiming the Sir Richard Hadlee Medal as New Zealand’s top player in 2025 and making the final of this year’s T20 World Cup in India before winning the IPL with Royal Challengers Bengaluru.
He made his test debut last year at the age of 31 but missed the mid-year tour of England and the one-off test against Ireland to be home with his wife for the birth of their first child.
The absence from the test setup has made him doubly keen to tear into India with the red ball ahead of a four-test tour of Australia.
“I’ve played four tests in my life. I get up for any test. There’s something special about them,” he said.

title: PHC issues notices in plea against emergency, governor’s rule in KP
text:
PHC issues notices in plea against emergency, governor’s rule in KP
- Seeks replies from federal govt, police on Sohail Afridi’s whereabouts
The Peshawar High Court has issued notices challenging governor's rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and seeking the recovery of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, with responses due within two days.
- PHC's challenge to governor's rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
- Court's demand for information on CM Sohail Afridi's alleged detention.
- Arguments questioning the constitutionality of the presidential proclamation.
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) has issued notices to the federal government, the attorney general, police and other relevant authorities on petitions challenging the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, as well as a plea seeking the recovery of non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, Aaj News reported on Tuesday.
The court sought a formal response from the authorities within two days regarding Afridi’s alleged detention. Further hearing of the petition challenging the emergency and governor’s rule was adjourned until November 10.
During the hearing on Afridi’s recovery plea, Justice Syed Arshad Ali asked about his whereabouts. The petitioner’s counsel told the court that Afridi had been detained following the imposition of governor’s rule and the emergency, adding that reports suggested he was being held at the “Shahi Mehman Khana” at one of two possible locations.
After hearing the arguments, the court directed the relevant authorities to submit their replies within two days.
Separately, a bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Faheem Wali heard the main petition filed by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan.
The petition seeks to have the presidential proclamation issued on October 11, the imposition of the emergency and governor’s rule, and orders for the deployment of the armed forces declared unconstitutional and set aside.
The petitioner’s counsel argued that the Constitution required a resolution from the provincial assembly for the imposition of an emergency. He also contended that governor’s rule had been imposed across the province despite improvements in the law and order situation in Peshawar, Nowshera and Mardan.
Speaking to the media after the proceedings, Barrister Gohar alleged that the elected provincial government had been removed under the pretext of terrorism. He claimed that 12 PTI members of the National Assembly and 14 members of the provincial assembly had been detained.
He demanded the immediate release of Afridi and the other detained lawmakers.
Meanwhile, Salman Akram Raja and Mahmood Khan Achakzai also described governor’s rule as an attack on provincial autonomy and vowed to continue peaceful resistance within the bounds of the Constitution and law.

title: Makkah Defence Alliance: Any attack on KSA will trigger collective response: DG ISPR
text:
RAWALPINDI: Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt-General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to reducing regional tensions through diplomatic engagement with Iran while warning that any threat to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity or Islamic holy sites would face a collective response under the Makkah Defence Alliance.
In an Interview with Independent Arabia, Lt-Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that “the concern about escalation is always present because we are witnessing a recurring cycle of de-escalation and escalation, then de-escalation and escalation again,” explaining that Pakistan and its partners in the region continue to engage with the relevant parties to try to break this cycle.
He added, “We constantly emphasise to them that this cycle is not good, and it does not serve the interests of the region, nor the interests of the parties involved in the conflict itself,” stressing that Islamabad will continue its diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions.
The military spokesperson said Pakistan was maintaining communication with Tehran and other regional stakeholders to prevent further escalation and pursue peaceful solutions to ongoing conflicts. He also confirmed that the collective deterrence mechanism established under the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Türkiye defence arrangement was already being implemented, describing it as a defensive framework intended to discourage aggression and preserve regional stability.
Discussing Pakistan’s communication with Iran, the ISPR DG said the country’s political and military leadership had maintained contacts with Tehran for several months, focusing on restraint and preventing further escalation. He explained that Pakistan’s engagement with the relevant parties was aimed at narrowing differences and encouraging negotiated solutions rather than allowing the conflict to expand.
He said Pakistan and its regional partners were working to prevent the conflict from expanding geographically or intensifying militarily.
When asked whether Islamabad had conveyed a direct warning to Tehran following the attacks on Saudi Arabia, he neither confirmed nor denied such communication. However, he emphasised that Pakistan’s diplomatic exchanges remained focused on reducing tensions.
The military spokesperson also warned that continued regional confrontation would not serve the interests of the countries involved, stressing the importance of negotiations and diplomatic engagement.
The ISPR DG reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to protecting Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and the security of the Two Holy Mosques. He said Pakistan was already providing the necessary support to Saudi Arabia and would continue doing so under its existing defence commitments.
While declining to disclose operational details because of military confidentiality, he maintained that Islamabad remained prepared to employ the means available to fulfil its security obligations.
His remarks came against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, which have raised concerns about regional security and the protection of Islamic holy sites.
The DG ISPR said the attacks had generated anger among Pakistan’s political and military leadership and the wider public, reflecting the importance attached to the security of Makkah and Madinah.
Explaining the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Türkiye defence arrangement, Lt-Gen Chaudhry described the Makkah Alliance as a defensive mechanism grounded in the right of self-defence under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter.
He said the alliance was not directed against any particular country and had no offensive objectives. Instead, its purpose was to strengthen collective security, discourage aggression and support regional peace.
According to the ISPR DG, any direct or indirect war against one of the three member countries would trigger a collective response under the alliance’s commitments. He also highlighted progress in the alliance’s institutional development, including the establishment of its secretariat and a strategic political and defence committee involving senior officials from the three countries.
Lt-Gen Chaudhry said the arrangement built upon longstanding defence cooperation and historical relations among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye. He further clarified that the alliance did not replace existing bilateral defence agreements or security partnerships.
Addressing those responsible for attacks against Saudi Arabia, the military spokesperson said Pakistan’s defence commitments were intended to send an unmistakable message to both the perpetrators and those supporting them.
He stressed that the collective deterrence framework was designed to demonstrate the willingness and capability of member countries to respond to threats.
Referring to Pakistan’s experience in dealing with non-state armed groups, Lt Gen Chaudhry argued that such organisations often operated differently from states and could be difficult to deter through conventional diplomatic signals alone.
He maintained that clear and decisive security commitments were necessary to discourage further attacks and prevent militant groups from exploiting regional instability.
The ISPR DG also cautioned that expanding military confrontation would harm regional interests and complicate efforts to reach negotiated settlements.
Discussing the future of the Makkah Alliance, Lt-Gen Chaudhry said the arrangement was not necessarily limited to its three founding members. He indicated that countries sharing its objectives of regional stability and collective security could potentially become part of the framework.
However, he did not confirm reports concerning the possible inclusion of other countries, explaining that decisions about membership rested with the political and strategic leadership of the existing member states.
The military spokesperson reiterated that the alliance was intended to promote peace and security rather than create confrontation with any particular regional actor.
The ISPR DG also discussed maritime security challenges in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, highlighting the importance of international cooperation to protect shipping routes and regional trade.
He referred to Pakistan’s participation in multinational maritime security arrangements and said regional countries were increasingly recognising the importance of collective security cooperation.

title: New Saudi envoy, CDF take stock of regional situation
text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on Monday expressed satisfaction over progress made under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening defence cooperation, institutional linkages and strategic coordination.

Field Marshal Asim Munir congratulated the Saudi Ambassador on his appointment and expressed confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
Both sides reaffirmed the importance of their strategic partnership, rooted in shared faith, mutual trust and close bilateral cooperation.

title: NA session: Achakzai demands govt disclose Afridi’s whereabouts
text:
ISLAMABAD: Opposition leader in National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai on Monday demanded of the government to immediately disclose the whereabouts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and others who have been missing since the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in the province on October 11.
Speaking in National Assembly, the PTI-backed opposition leader demanded the immediate production of Chief Minister Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Salim Swati and six PTI MNAs, whose whereabouts remain unknown since what he termed the October 11 “black day”.
As Achakzai took the floor, the National Assembly’s YouTube livestream appeared to blur, prompting PTI lawmakers to accuse the government of presiding over what they called a “Form 47 regime” that feared facing its critics.
Questioning the government’s failure to provide information about the chief minister’s whereabouts, Achakzai asked whether the authorities could even confirm that he was alive.
“We have repeatedly requested that we be told where the KP chief minister is. Is he even alive or not? Where are the PA speaker and the six PTI MNAs,” he asked. “Fine, you have picked him up, but at least tell us where he is.”
He also demanded production orders for the six MNAs, arguing that ensuring the presence of elected representatives in parliament was a right rather than a concession from the government.
“If someone is a member of parliament, obtaining his production order and defending him is your right, Mr Speaker,” he said.
Achakzai maintained that even if a parliamentarian had been detained, parliamentary privileges should be respected and arrangements made for the member’s appearance before the House.
Rejecting the government’s legislative agenda, he said the opposition would resist any legislation it considered contrary to democratic principles and the Constitution.
“Make whatever laws you want to make,” he said. “We want nothing from you. Keep one thing in mind: we will resist any legislation that goes against democratic norms and the Constitution.”
Referring to protests abroad, Achakzai cited recent demonstrations in France over inflation, claiming that millions had taken to the streets without being subjected to gunfire.
He contrasted what he described as the restraint shown by French authorities with the Pakistani government’s handling of political dissent, alleging that the latter had resorted to killings.
He also referred to expressions of support for the French protesters in Berlin, urging the authorities to learn from international protest movements and address public grievances without resorting to force.
Warning of possible unrest in Pakistan, Achakzai said the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in KP, where he said the provincial government had a two-thirds majority, raised serious constitutional concerns.
He cautioned that continued measures he considered unconstitutional could eventually drive people onto the streets.
Concluding his remarks, Achakzai reiterated the opposition’s demands for constitutional supremacy, parliamentary sovereignty and genuine democratic elections.
“The supremacy of the Constitution, parliament as the source of power, and genuine democratic elections are our demands,” he said. “We don’t want any development schemes from you.”
Meanwhile, talking to reporters, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan rejected reports that the party’s core committee wanted Achakzai to step down as opposition leader in National Assembly, making it clear that no one could challenge party’s founding chairman Imran Khan’s decisions.
“Imran Khan appointed Achakzai as the opposition leader and he will remain our opposition leader. No one can defy Khan’s decisions,” he declared.

title: Emergency and governor’s rule in KP: PTI vows to resist ‘curbs’ through public mobilisation
text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Monday rejected the recent imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terming the measures an unconstitutional assault on the public mandate, and vowed to resist them through legal, parliamentary and peaceful public mobilisation.
In a unanimous declaration issued after a two-day joint meeting of its political committee and core committee, the party condemned the actions taken on October 11, including the establishment of a council and measures it said were intended to render the elected provincial government ineffective or dissolve it.
PTI argued that politically undermining an elected government would revive authoritarian practices associated with the country’s past, drawing parallels with the repealed Article 58(2)(b) of the Constitution.
It said the measures violated constitutional supremacy, provincial autonomy, federalism and democratic principles, and declared it would not accept them.
PTI condemned the alleged abduction and illegal detention of the KP chief minister, assembly speaker, ministers and lawmakers, demanding their immediate recovery, protection of their legal rights and action against those responsible.
PTI also raised concerns over the treatment of Imran Khan’s three sisters, alleging that their grievances had remained unresolved for a month and demanding protection of their fundamental, constitutional and legal rights.
The declaration accused authorities of conducting a nationwide crackdown on PTI leaders, office-bearers, workers and supporters through raids, arrests, harassment and politically motivated detentions.
According to figures presented at the meeting, more than 1,500 party workers were arrested during the street movement in Punjab. Hundreds were subsequently detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO), particularly Section 3, while several remained imprisoned, the party claimed.
PTI alleged that workers whose MPO detention periods were expiring were being rearrested under fresh orders instead of being released.
It termed the practice an abuse of legal powers, a violation of civil liberties and an organised campaign of political retaliation.
The party also condemned continued detentions of workers arrested during the movement in Sindh, alleging that supporters remained imprisoned or held under MPO orders. It extended its condemnation to arrests in KP, Balochistan and Islamabad, as well as raids on the homes of party leaders, workers and their families.
The meeting reviewed what PTI described as violations of the fundamental rights of incarcerated party chairman Imran Khan and other political prisoners, demanding protection of their constitutional and legal entitlements.
The party alleged that arrests and harassment had intensified after the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, linking the actions to political retaliation.
PTI vowed to challenge the measures on all constitutional, legal, parliamentary and peaceful public platforms.

title: Health Secy visits PIMS Hospital to review action plan
text:
ISLAMABAD: Federal Health Secretary Nadeem Mahbub on Monday visited Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) Hospital to review the future action plan for resolving the hospital’s administrative and operational matters on a priority basis.
The secretary reviewed the situation of increasing number of patients at PIMS and the status of available staff; review of PIMS development projects and Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) affairs.
The Federal Health Secretary also visited the new emergency department and reviewed ongoing preparations to make the new emergency operational which has already been delayed over a year. Mahbub directed the administration to timely complete the facility, so that the additional patients can easily be treated at the 200 bed facility. The Health Secretary directed that steps to make the new emergency operational be accelerated.
A briefing was also given on the ongoing measures for staff recruitment for the new emergency services. The Health Secretary ensured that PIMS’ administrative and operational issues would be resolved on a priority basis.
Mahbub directed to further improve medical facilities and administrative affairs at PIMS. The Health Secretary stated that effective management of human resources in the hospital should be ensured in accordance with high standards, and the provision of maximum facilities to patients and general citizens must be ensured.
During the visit, the Executive Director of PIMS, the Joint Executive Director of PIMS, and heads of various departments of the hospital were also present.

title: IBA, AKU, HU collaborate to advance AI-driven teaching, learning
text:

The symposium brought together academic leaders, educators, researchers, and teaching professionals from Karachi, across Pakistan, and internationally to explore the opportunities and challenges artificial intelligence presents for higher education.

title: 7th poliovirus case of the year reported at Karachi East
text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has reported its seventh poliovirus case of the current year, from Karachi East district in Sindh, underscoring the urgent need for consistent vaccination to protect children against a paralytic disease that has no cure but can be prevented through vaccination.
According to the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication (NEOC) the case was reported through the polio surveillance network and confirmed by the Regional Reference Laboratory for Polio Eradication at the National Institute of Health (NIH).
A comprehensive case investigation has already been launched. The Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI) is already analyzing the best science-based response to tackle and prevent further transmission, including targeted vaccination activities and support to strengthen routine immunization.
The last case from Karachi was reported in December 2024. Despite an overall decline in wild poliovirus transmission, the Karachi has continued to report environmental detections throughout the year, indicating that ongoing transmission remains a real threat for children.
Owing to mass polio vaccination drives—which are safe and effective—Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8 percent, from an estimated 20,000 cases in the early 1990s to 31 in 2025, and seven so far this year. Of this year’s seven reported cases, five are from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (four from southern KP alone) and two are from Sindh.
In 2026, Pakistan has already implemented four large-scale polio campaigns, protecting more than 45 million children multiple times, alongside smaller targeted oral and injectable vaccination campaigns in high-risk areas. In September, a sub-national campaign protected over 29.3 million children across the country, while the next vaccination round is scheduled from November 2-8 to protect nearly 24 million in 97 districts, including all districts of Karachi.
Polio is a highly contagious and incurable disease that can cause lifelong paralysis and, in some cases, death. It can, however, be prevented through safe and effective polio vaccines, which have been used safely in 195 countries, including all Muslim-majority countries.
Polio eradication is a collective responsibility. Pakistan’s dedicated frontline workers continue to bring vaccines to children at their doorsteps, while parents and caregivers play a crucial role by ensuring their children receive all recommended doses, including routine immunizations. The PEI urges all parents and communities to ensure that all children under five receive the protective polio vaccine in every round.
Communities, religious leaders, and the media also have a vital role to play in promoting vaccination, countering misinformation, and ensuring every child is reached. Together, we can build a healthier Pakistan for all and achieve a polio-free future for every family, regardless of social or economic status, no matter where they live or who they are.

title: Workers' welfare, protection of rights among Govt's top priorities: Salik
text:
Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Chaudhry Salik Hussain has said that the welfare of workers, protection of their rights and provision of quality education to their children are among the government’s top priorities.
Workers’ welfare, protection of rights among Govt’s top priorities: Salik
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Chaudhry Salik Hussain has said that the welfare of workers, protection of their rights and provision of quality education to their children are among the government’s top priorities.
“Respect for the worker is respect for Pakistan. When labourers prosper, Pakistan prospers,” the Federal Minister said while addressing the Foundation Stone laying ceremony of Labour Complex Phase-II in Taxila.
The ceremony was attended by Minister of State for Law and Justice Barrister Aqeel Ahmed Malik, Member of the Provincial Assembly Mohsin Ayub Khan, former MPA Haji Malik Umar Farooq, Secretary Workers Welfare Fund Zulfiqar Ahmed, Central Information Secretary of Pakistan Muslim League (Q) Ghulam Mustafa Malik, President Federal Capital Rizwan Sadiq, President Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Intikhab Khan Chamkani, board members, senior officials and representatives of political and social circles.
Chaudhry Salik Hussain said that the total approved cost of Labour Complex Phase-II was Rs1.106 billion, and the project would be completed within, and preferably before, the stipulated period of 24 months.
The project includes the construction of high schools for boys and girls, a junior primary school, a mosque and a mini market, he said.
The Federal Minister further said that 504 flats had already been constructed at the Labour Complex Taxila at a cost of Rs1.314 billion. Out of these, 70 flats had been earmarked for the families of martyrs of Pakistan Ordnance Factories (POF), Wah Cantt.
He said the government was giving high priority to handing over the completed flats to deserving labour families at the earliest. Coordination with the relevant ministries and authorities was underway to complete the necessary formalities and hand over the keys to the eligible families.
Chaudhry Salik Hussain expressed hope that effective progress would be made in this regard during the coming weeks so that the process of handing over the flats could be taken forward without further delay.
Speaking about public service, the Federal Minister said he considered politics a form of virtue and believed that serving the people was the fundamental purpose of holding public office.
He said politicians should not wait for another opportunity, ministry or position to take measures for public welfare. Instead, they should consider every day valuable and fulfil their responsibilities with sincerity and dedication.
“Power is not permanent. Therefore, whenever an opportunity to serve the people is available, it should not be wasted,” he said, adding that resolving even one deserving person’s problem and earning the prayers of a needy individual was a significant achievement.
The Federal Minister directed the concerned authorities to ensure high construction standards, transparency and timely completion of the Labour Complex Phase-II project.
“When the labourer is prosperous, Pakistan will be prosperous,” Chaudhry Salik Hussain reiterated.

title: KP emergency, governor’s rule aimed at restoring peace: Dr.Tariq
text:
Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhary on Tuesday said the imposition of emergency and Governor’s Rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa followed the provincial government’s lack of cooperation with the federal government and state institutions in the fight against terrorism.
KP emergency, governor’s rule aimed at restoring peace: Dr.Tariq
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhary on Tuesday said the imposition of emergency and Governor’s Rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa followed the provincial government’s lack of cooperation with the federal government and state institutions in the fight against terrorism.
Addressing a press conference, he said emergency and Governor’s Rule were imposed through a presidential order on October 11 under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, respectively. Both measures were subsequently endorsed by Parliament and a joint sitting, completing the constitutional requirements, he added.
He said Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had assumed the powers of the provincial government, while an 11-member advisory council comprising highly qualified professionals with distinguished records in their respective fields had been constituted to assist him.
Local tribal elders had also been included in councils formed for 12 terrorism-affected districts to ensure community participation in consultations and intelligence-based operations.
Dr Tariq Fazal said the imposition of emergency might have been avoided had the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government cooperated with the federal government, state institutions, law enforcement agencies and security forces in counterterrorism efforts.
He recalled that during negotiations held in Islamabad on the prime minister’s direction, the federal government had sought the provincial government’s cooperation and assurances regarding counterterrorism measures.
The minister said terrorism had affected the entire country and could not be controlled without full cooperation between the provincial government, federal institutions, the armed forces and security agencies.
He added that terrorist incidents had increased significantly, particularly over the past two years, while personnel and officers of the armed forces, police and Frontier Corps continued to sacrifice their lives in counterterrorism operations.
He said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had contacted the provincial leadership several times through back-channel communications to seek cooperation, with some contacts reported in the media and others remaining unreported.
However, he said that the provincial government’s non-cooperation had continued, leaving the federal government with no option but to take the decision.
Dr Tariq Fazal also identified cross-border infiltration from Afghanistan as a major security challenge and alleged that the provincial government had refused to cooperate with the federal government’s policy to address the issue.
He said the federal government possessed information about the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa beyond what had been reported in the media and was committed, alongside the security forces, to controlling infiltration and eliminating terrorism.
The minister urged all opposition parties to develop a political consensus against terrorism, saying national security, peace and the future of Pakistan’s children must remain above political differences.
He said he had invited opposition parties for talks the previous day and was reiterating his call for them to sit together and formulate a joint strategy against terrorism.
“Why can’t we develop a consensus on at least one issue that is directly linked to the country’s peace and the future of its children?” he asked, urging political parties to join hands with the federal government in the fight against terrorism.
Criticising PTI, Dr Tariq Fazal said the party had remained in power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for 12 to 13 years but had been unable to establish the desired level of peace, particularly over the past two to two-and-a-half years.
He questioned the party’s approach to counterterrorism, saying security personnel were sacrificing their lives while political activities and protests continued on the streets. He urged the PTI leadership to reconsider its position, engage with the federal government and develop consensus on counterterrorism efforts.
He said intelligence-based operations were already under way in the province and called on opposition parties to participate in these efforts rather than oppose them.
Referring to previous negotiations between the government and opposition, Dr Tariq Fazal said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had invited the opposition for talks and the government had participated in the process sincerely.
He said representatives of both sides had held extensive discussions over two days, working on several drafts until around 2:30am. According to him, the government had incorporated the opposition’s proposals into the draft agreement, but the opposition leadership ultimately rejected it.
He clarified that his criticism was not directed at the six opposition representatives who participated in the negotiations. Instead, he questioned the role of the broader opposition leadership in rejecting the proposed agreement.
The minister said the negotiations had initially proposed imposing emergency measures in 12 terrorism-affected districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to facilitate cooperation between the provincial and federal governments in restoring peace.
The proposal was subsequently narrowed to five districts, where the opposition was asked to cooperate with law enforcement agencies and support operations against terrorists. However, he said, the opposition had not accepted even the revised proposal.
Questioning the provincial government’s approach, he asked whether restoring peace in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was solely the federal government’s responsibility.
He said provincial governments facing terrorism generally sought additional federal security personnel, resources and intelligence-based operations, whereas the federal government had repeatedly urged the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government to cooperate with law enforcement agencies.
Dr Tariq Fazal reiterated that the government remained ready to resume negotiations. He said the prime minister had again extended an invitation to the opposition from the floor of the House, making it clear that talks could take place if the opposition was willing.
Comparing the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Balochistan, the minister said terrorism was also a serious challenge in the latter province, but its provincial administration and chief minister were cooperating with federal institutions and law enforcement agencies in the fight against militants.
He said the Balochistan chief minister was confronting terrorists on the front line and cooperating with security agencies rather than refusing to participate in counterterrorism operations. He described this difference between the approaches of the two provincial administrations as significant in addressing the country’s security challenges.
He expressed regret that some people were linking the imposition of emergency and Governor’s Rule to other issues, including mineral resources.
The minister said the people of a province had the first right to benefit from its natural resources. International companies involved in joint exploration projects, he added, were expected to follow international standards and ensure that exploration activities did not create difficulties for local communities.
He said all four provinces needed further investment in education and healthcare, adding that revenues generated from natural resources, including minerals, oil and gas, could help finance development and improve public services. However, he stressed that political consensus and a conducive environment were essential for effectively utilising these resources.
He also said Pakistan was being recognised internationally as a regional stabilising force, referring to the efforts of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir. He urged political parties not to undermine the country’s progress through political confrontation.
He expressed confidence that lasting peace would eventually be established in the province, paving the way for development and prosperity.
 “We can sacrifice politics, but we cannot sacrifice the state, national interests or state institutions,” he said, reaffirming the government’s commitment to national security, stability and development.

title: IHC makes key administrative changes; registrar, inspection team member relieved of duties
text:
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has made key administrative changes, relieving Registrar Yar Muhammad Walanah and Member Inspection Team Tanveer Akbar of their positions. title: SVI hosts two-day Non-Proliferation Conference - 2026
text:
The Strategic Vision Institute (SVI), Islamabad, hosts the second iteration of Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference 2026, a two-day international event bringing together a distinguished group of scholars and experts from around the world.
SVI hosts two-day Non-Proliferation Conference – 2026
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):The Strategic Vision Institute (SVI), Islamabad, hosts the second iteration of Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference 2026, a two-day international event bringing together a distinguished group of scholars and experts from around the world.
The conference aims at fostering constructive dialogue on global strategic issues and sharing Pakistan’s policy perspectives.  Dr Naeem Salik, Executive Director (ED), SVI, welcomed the distinguished guests to the International Nonproliferation Conference (INC) 2026. Dr Nasir Hafeez, Director, SVI, subsequently introduced the conference to the esteemed audience.
The inaugural address was delivered by Lt. Gen. Sarfraz Sattar, HI (M), (Retd.), Advisor, NCA. He mentioned that the disruptive technologies sit at the heart of the push towards bigger and better Nuclear Weapons, against the efforts of restraint or stability on the road to disarmament and sustained economic development.
He said, that there has been a shift in the nuclear age marked by the change of threat perception from rouge or non-state actors getting access to nuclear weapons towards the challenge of Great Power Competition and the possibility of interstate conflict in a more contested international system.
He mentioned South Asia as a nuclear flashpoint, owing to India’s ultranationalist tendencies. We face Hindutva ideology which is in pursuit of Akhand Bharat. He further mentioned that the nuclear non-use taboo seems to be weakening as we see the likelihood of interstate wars increasing both in lethality and expense. The sole function of global nuclear order is also under extreme stress.
Lt. Gen. Khalid Ahmed Kidwai, (Retd.), Advisor Development, National Command Authority (NCA), delivered the keynote address. He examined Pakistan’s perspective on credible deterrence, strategic balance, and strategic stability in South Asia, tracing their evolution in the pre-May 2025 conflict period and assessing their implications in the post-conflict strategic environment. Lt Gen. Kidwai (Retd.) emphasized that Pakistan’s Full Spectrum Deterrence (FSD) is fundamentally defensive, aimed at preventing aggression across the entire spectrum of conflict and preserving strategic stability in South Asia. Pakistan’s Full Spectrum Deterrence generated strategic effects in both regional and international arenas in the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, as the role of conventional and nuclear deterrence in limiting escalation was demonstrated. He highlighted SIPRI Yearbook 2026 findings on India’s deployment of approximately 12 nuclear warheads aboard a nuclear submarine for deterrence patrols, expressing concern that the absence of pre-notification of Indian SLBM tests could undermine South Asian strategic stability, raise questions about India’s NFU policy, and increase the risks of miscalculation and nuclear escalation. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s right to take appropriate measures to safeguard its national security and preserve the regional strategic balance. Furthermore, he stressed the importance of preventing technological imbalances from undermining strategic stability in South Asia.
To comprehensively address the spectrum of challenges, the conference hosts seven working sessions on critical topics such as deterrence dynamics and escalation risks in South Asia, the evolving deterrence landscape in a transforming global nuclear order, and the collapse of the arms control architecture and challenges to the non-proliferation regime. Each session facilitates in-depth discussions, aiming at generating policy-relevant recommendations in both national and global security frameworks. The conference will be concluded with an address by Gen. Zubair Mahmood Hayat, NI (M), (Retd.), Former Chairman, Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee (CJCSC).

Ashrafi, IIUI President discuss countering ideological terrorism through youth awareness
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Chairman of the Pakistan Ulema Council, Secretary-General of the International Tazeem-e-Haramain Sharifain Council and Coordinator of the National Paigham-e-Aman Committee, Hafiz Muhammad Tahir Mehmood Ashrafi, on Tuesday held a meeting with President of the International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI), Prof. Dr. Ahmed Saad Alahmed, at his office and discussed the issues of mutual interests including ideological terrorism, youth awareness and efforts to promote religious harmony.
During the meeting, the two dignitaries discussed the growing challenge of ideological terrorism, emphasizing the need to address the ideas and narratives that fuel extremism.
They observed that ideological terrorism could be more dangerous than other forms of terrorism and stressed the importance of raising awareness among young people to help them understand and counter this social menace.
The meeting also featured a briefing on the National Paigham-e-Aman Committee and its efforts to promote intrafaith and interfaith harmony across Pakistan.
The committee’s role in fostering understanding, peaceful coexistence and cooperation among different religious communities was highlighted.
Ashrafi underscored the importance of engaging young people in awareness initiatives and promoting dialogue and mutual respect as part of broader efforts to counter extremist ideologies and strengthen social harmony.
He also appreciated Saudi Arabia’s cooperation in the education sector and acknowledged the continued support extended to Pakistan by the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud in various spheres of life.
Concluding his remarks, Ashrafi condemned the Houthi attacks in his strongest terms on the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including airports, oil facilities and the holy sites.
He reaffirmed his full support on behalf of the Pakistan Ulema Council and its allied parties to the Kingdom and its leadership through thick and thin and reiterated its commitment that the security and sovereignty of the Haramain Sharifain is the redline for them and Pakistan.
He assured that there will be no compromise on the safety and integrity of the Saudi Arabia under all circumstances.
They underscored the importance of cooperation among religious scholars, educational institutions and relevant organisations in addressing ideological extremism, promoting awareness among youth and strengthening interfaith and intrafaith harmony.

title: BISP introduces interoperability in Digital Wallet Payments, enabling withdrawals from any authorized retailer
text:
Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) Chairperson Senator Rubina Khalid on Tuesday said women beneficiaries would be able to withdraw their funds from any authorized retailer of six partner banks in any city across Pakistan, on any day and at any time, following the introduction of interoperability in digital wallet payments.
BISP introduces interoperability in Digital Wallet Payments, enabling withdrawals from any authorized retailer
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) Chairperson Senator Rubina Khalid on Tuesday said women beneficiaries would be able to withdraw their funds from any authorized retailer of six partner banks in any city across Pakistan, on any day and at any time, following the introduction of interoperability in digital wallet payments.
She made these remarks while listening to the concerns of 28 callers during a live E-Kachehri held at BISP Headquarters, directing the relevant officials to resolve their complaints on a priority basis.
Senator Rubina Khalid said the interoperability feature would remove restrictions on beneficiaries withdrawing funds through a particular bank or within a specific city, providing them greater flexibility and convenience in accessing their payments.
The six partner banks include HBL, Habib Microfinance, Bank Alfalah, Telenor Microfinance, Bank of Punjab and Mobilink/Jazz Bank.
She said the digital wallet payment system had been introduced on the directives of President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif to ensure secure and transparent payments to women beneficiaries.
The chairperson advised beneficiaries to obtain their free Benazir SIMs exclusively from BISP offices.
They must bring their original Computerized National Identity Cards (CNICs) and personal mobile phones to collect the SIMs. Activation would be carried out by a representative of the relevant mobile network operator at the BISP office or designated site.
She also advised women beneficiaries to retain confirmation messages received after fund transfers and withdrawals for their records and cautioned them against handing over their mobile phones to retailers or agents during cash withdrawals.
She emphasized that an original CNIC and biometric verification would be mandatory for withdrawing funds.
Senator Rubina Khalid further urged women beneficiaries whose CNICs had expired to renew them through the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) without delay.
Clarifying the survey process, she said household eligibility was determined through the BISP survey and that a repeat survey could not be conducted until two years had elapsed since the previous survey.
She advised women not to visit BISP offices repeatedly to request a new survey before completion of the stipulated period.

title: KP’s worsening security situation demands action against terrorism: Danyal Chaudhry
text:
Federal Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Broadcasting, Barrister Danyal Chaudhry, on Tesday said that conditions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had been worsening for years, while the provincial leadership had failed to take effective measures against terrorism.
KP’s worsening security situation demands action against terrorism: Danyal Chaudhry
ISLAMABAD, Oct 20 (APP):Federal Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Broadcasting, Barrister Danyal Chaudhry, on Tesday said that conditions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had been worsening for years, while the provincial leadership had failed to take effective measures against terrorism.
Talking to the media outside the Parliament House, he said the government had continued negotiations with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf  (PTI) until the last moment in an effort to resolve the issue through dialogue.
He said that governor’s rule or emergency was the least preferred option for any democratic government, but the sacrifices of martyrs and the rise in terrorism had compelled the government to take this step.
He said that personnel of law enforcement agencies were being martyred daily in the fight against terrorism, while their families, widows and orphaned children repeatedly asked how many more children would be orphaned and how many more mothers would be separated from their loved ones.
He said PTI was repeatedly asked to give a practical commitment against terrorism, but no satisfactory response was received.
He said that coffins draped in the Pakistani flag were arriving daily in Rawalpindi and other areas, while negotiations with terrorists and a policy of leniency had further worsened the situation.
Barrister Danyal Chaudhry raised several questions regarding Maulana Fazlur Rehman and said that PTI had previously levelled various allegations against him, including those relating to permits, land of martyrs, training camps and support for terrorists.
He asked whether those allegations were wrong at the time or whether Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s current defence of PTI was wrong.
He said Maulana Fazlur Rehman had described PTI in 2012 as the creation of Jews and Western powers, while in 2021 he alleged that PTI founder and his party had received foreign funding.
He said that in 2023, Maulana had claimed that foreign agencies had used PTI founder to bring him into power.
Barrister Danyal Chaudhry said Maulana Fazlur Rehman had alleged in November 2022 that foreign funding was intended to support the long march and to cancel the visit of the Chinese president.
He said Maulana Fazlur Rehman had described the May 2023 incidents as an attempt to demoralize the martyrs of the armed forces and weaken Pakistan’s military.
He asked that if these statements were correct, what was the basis for standing in defence of PTI today.
Barrister Danyal Chaudhry said that a sudden change in Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s political position after two decades suggested some personal or political interest, as no such change could outweigh the funerals of martyrs, their sacrifices and national security.
He said if Maulana’s past statements were wrong, he should clarify his position before the nation.
He said allegations that the government had taken mines and mineral “Madianities” or made a decision under any agreement were baseless, as governor’s rule was imposed not because of any deal or political pressure, but in view of the sacrifices of martyrs, the increase in terrorism and the requirements of national security.
Barrister called upon Maulana Fazlur Rehman to explain the difference between the situations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, saying that there were fundamental differences between terrorism, insurgency and the policies of the provincial governments in both provinces.
He said the Balochistan government had supported the state’s position against terrorism, whereas the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government had adopted a position driven by its political interests.
He said Maulana Fazlur Rehman and his party would have to provide clear answers to all these questions, as either their past statements were wrong or their current position was wrong.
He said the people and the families of martyrs wanted answers to these questions at the earliest.

title: EOC polio organizes engagement session with media; highlights objectives of upcoming IPV campaign
text:
Emergency Operation Center (EOC) polio Khyber Pakhtunkhwa here on Tuesday organized ‘Annual Engagement Session’ with media to highlight efforts being underway to eradicate polio and to apprise media about objectives of upcoming fIPV vaccination campaign.
EOC polio organizes engagement session with media; highlights objectives of upcoming IPV campaign
PESHAWAR, Oct 20 (APP):Emergency Operation Center (EOC) polio Khyber Pakhtunkhwa here on Tuesday organized ‘Annual Engagement Session’ with media to highlight efforts being underway to eradicate polio and to apprise media about objectives of upcoming fIPV vaccination campaign.
The event titled ” From Headlines to Life Lines : Reporting for a Polio-Free KP” was attended by EOC Coordinator, Sarah Rehman health experts, representatives of WHO and large number of media persons.
The session discussed achievements of anti polio campaigns, immunization landscape, epidemiological trends, program progress, challenges, strategies, social hurdles and the objectives of upcoming fPV vaccination drive.
Addressing the participants, Sarah Rehman praised media for its role in efforts against polio stressing that each and every segment of society should play its role in national cause of clearing society of polio. She said that even if a single door of house was opened for polio workers due to efforts of media it would be great success for us adding that it would further pave way to achieve the desired targets.
She said that we had to collectively work and change mindset of people, address social hurdles and remove misconception of people about polio vaccine. She said that upcoming IPV campaign would prove to be a way forward to eliminate polio from society and to save future of our coming generations. She also underscored the need of more coordinated and effective vaccination campaign in southern KP and its adjoining areas to protect population living in provincial metropolis.
Dr. Sardar Alam of WHO said that we were very close to polio eradication but last nail in coffin needs joint efforts, removing mistrust and proper awareness of people about polio disease.
He also informed participants about the reasons of polio virus existence and said it is reportedly endemic in certain areas while it survives and found in sewerage lines adding that virus become active when it comes into contact with humans. He said that polio cases are only reported in Pakistan and neighboring Afghanistan while the virus that is found in sewerage lines of Peshawar was of Nangarhar, Afghanistan origin.
He told that we are planning a supplementary program in addition to routine immunization campaign aiming complete polio eradication. He told that IPV and OPV vaccination campaign targets selective age group of 5 to 10 years to end ‘Chain Circulation’ of polio virus.
Communication Officer Polio UNICEF, Shadab Younas told that we want to change behavior and mindset of people as it is prerequisite to wipe out polio. She said that we have changed strategies due to diversity of communities adding that we aims to engage maximum number of people to achieve desired results of polio vaccination campaigns.
The salaries of polio workers have been increased and steps have been taken for their capacity building enabling them to cope with existing situations. She also urged media to report evidence based news, counter misinformation, amplify efforts of front line workers and utilize all available social media tools for people awareness about importance of vaccination campaigns.
